why: The new C9 binding kept negation/polarity/quantifier tokens glued to their immediately following scope, so the model stopped cutting right after those tokens (giving small gains for very short pieces, ≤3 and ≤5). That avoidance pushed cuts elsewhere — often earlier or inside enumerations — which increased fragmentation and contradiction risk for mid/long spans (the ≤7 and ≤99 bins).
lesson: A later revision should respect that the narrow polarity/quantifier binding helps very short pieces but can redistribute cuts into medium/long spans (producing isolated function words or broken enumerations), and so must avoid inducing that fragmentation.
